target: calyx (PO_0009060) as part of a qualified whole (pattern 12): whole flower (PO_0009046) with male (PATO_0000384); equivalently part of staminate flower (PO_0025600)
reason: Narrower: the calyx of a staminate flower. The sex is a quality of the flower, not the calyx, so this is pattern 12 as for 'female ovule' (R3072); no new class.

target: pedicel (PO_0030112) with the whole flower (PO_0009046) qualified male (PATO_0000384), pattern 12
reason: Narrower: the pedicel of a staminate flower. 'staminate' is in the reviewed context words for flowers, not pedicels. Caveat: in PO a pedicel supports a flower and is not part of it, so pattern 12 reads it loosely. Pattern 12 does not check parthood.

Generic part, like the earlier rejected 'segment' and 'wing'. The lobe may belong to a corolla, calyx, labellum or leaf. With the organ known it is that organ's lobe class (corolla lobe FLOPO_0986006, calyx lobe FLOPO_0986005, labellum lobe FLOPO_0986028) plus 'lower' FLOPO_0991377 through the context words.

target: corona lobe (FLOPO_0986035) with outer (FLOPO_0991379), pattern 04 position in a series
reason: Narrower: the outer member of a corona with two series of lobes. 'outer' is a reviewed series word for lobes.

target: portion of secretory tissue (PO_0005656) with container leaf lamina base (PO_0008019)
reason: Narrower: a gland ('gland' is mapped to PO_0005656) at the base of the leaf blade, as in Euphorbiaceae. It is a part with a fixed whole, like 'stipular colleter'. Counts go through pattern 03 with the lamina base as container.

target: plant organ base (FLOPO_0985024) part of pinnule (FLOPO_0985028)
reason: A region of an existing class, built the same way as 'style base' (R3670). Cuneate, truncate and cordate are base shapes.

target: bud scale leaf (PO_0020054) with basal (FLOPO_0991002), pattern 04
reason: Narrower: the lowest bud scales of a bud. 'basal' is a reviewed series word for scales; 'bud scale' is an exact PO synonym. Presence and absence go through pattern 15.

target: bract (PO_0009055) with outer (FLOPO_0991379), pattern 04
reason: Narrower: the outer series of an involucre or epicalyx ('5 bractées externes'). Read 'external' here as the series word 'outer'. The current context-word reading of 'external' as the outside surface is wrong for this part.

target: phyllome lamina lobe (PO_0025514) with container petal (PO_0009032)
reason: The filiform and linear segments, 8-10 per petal, are the divisions of a fringed or divided petal. This follows 'bract lobe' (R3665). Where a flora uses 'petal segment' for the whole petal, the bearer is petal PO_0009032.

target: leaf trichome (PO_0006504) with container leaf lamina margin (PO_0025009)
reason: Narrower: hairs or cilia on the leaf margin. 'hair' is a PO synonym of trichome. Some Portuguese and Spanish rows are marginal glands, which would be PO_0005656 instead.

target: corolla throat (FLOPO_0986110)
reason: Close to exact: the mouth is the distal opening of the corolla tube, i.e. the throat. Its diameter, obliquity and colour are qualities of the throat.

'Column' means the gynostemium (FLOPO_0986015) in orchids and the staminal tube or synandrium (FLOPO_0986013, FLOPO_0986014) in Malvaceae, Myristicaceae and Euphorbiaceae. The denticulate, discoid and crateriform apices point to the staminal column. Once the family has decided which column it is, the target is plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) part of that class.

target: asexual propagule (FLOPO_0986119)
reason: Exact: the Latinate singular of the existing FLOPO class. 'none' and 'sometimes present' go through pattern 15.

No class exists for 'ovary process', and the examples do not show which outgrowth of the ovary is meant. The margin could only be grounded on plant ovary, which would put denticulate and papillose margins on the ovary itself.

target: trichome (PO_0000282) with container hypanthium (PO_0009065)
reason: Narrower: hairs on the floral tube, which is the hypanthium in the families that use the term ('floral tube', R2246). Where the tube is the perianth tube, use FLOPO_0986010 as the container.

target: vascular leaf (PO_0009025) with upper (FLOPO_0991376), pattern 04
reason: Narrower: the uppermost leaves in the series on the stem. 'upper' is a reviewed series word for leaves.

target: shoot system (PO_0009006) with young (PATO_0000309), pattern 04
reason: Narrower: 'shoot' is a PO synonym of shoot system (as in 'leafy shoot', R2349), and 'young' is a reviewed bearer-quality word. Indumentum and colour of the new growth are qualities of the shoot.

target: plant ovary (PO_0009072) as part of a qualified whole (pattern 12): flower (PO_0009046) with female (PATO_0000383); equivalently part of pistillate flower (PO_0025599)
reason: Narrower: the ovary of a pistillate flower. The sex is a quality of the flower, so this is pattern 12 as for 'female ovule' (R3072).

Generic part: 'wing' was rejected in the 2026-11-13 review because it needs its organ. The examples include wings of seed chambers and fruits. With a known whole (seed wing FLOPO_0986091, anther wing FLOPO_0986137), add 'lateral' FLOPO_0991380 through pattern 04.

target: plant organ base (FLOPO_0985024) part of inflorescence axis (PO_0020122)
reason: In Andropogoneae (Hyparrhenia, Andropogon) the raceme-base is the short, often flattened and bearded stalk of a raceme, below its lowest spikelet pair. It is a region of the raceme axis. This is grass-only and found in 2 floras, so a rule is better than a new class.

target: secondary leaf vein (PO_0020140)
reason: Exact for the part, as in 'secondary veins per side' (R2833). 'per side' is the scope of the count (pattern 03 or 14).

target: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) part of style (PO_0009074)
reason: A region of the style. Where the 'tips' are the free divisions of a bifid style (lengths of 4-6 mm, recurved), the bearer is style branch FLOPO_0986008.

target: plant organ margin (PO_0025005) part of perigynium (PO_0009044), with winged (FLOPO_0985004 / reviewed 'winged')
reason: The wing of a Carex perigynium is a flange along its margin, so it is expressed on the perigynium margin. Most rows are 'width including wing', which is the width of the perigynium.

target: flower bract (PO_0009034)
reason: Narrower: the paleae (chaff) of an Asteraceae receptacle, each subtending a floret. Navicular, obovate and brown are palea qualities. This follows 'receptacle scale' (R2593).

target: involucre lobe (FLOPO_0986096) with container involucel (FLOPO_0986039)
reason: Narrower: an involucel is an involucre of a partial inflorescence, so its lobes are involucre lobes of that whole. A part with a fixed whole; no new class.

target: branch (PO_0025073)
reason: Narrower: a leaf-bearing branch. This follows 'leafy twig' (R2838). In mosses (complanate, julaceous) it is a branch of the gametophore. 'primary' is a series position, and 'pairs' is a count.

label: awn column
parent: is_a PO_0025001 (cardinal organ part); part_of PO_0025349 (awn)
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is the proximal, usually twisted portion of a geniculate awn (PO:0025349), from its base to the (first) bend.
reason: A real structure that grass floras (Stipeae, Aveneae, Andropogoneae, Aristida) describe on its own: its length to the first bend, twisting and hairs. It is not the awn base, since it runs to the bend and is 1.5-1.8 cm long. It is the counterpart of the distal awn limb (subula). Propose it to PO upstream.

target: plant organ margin (PO_0025005) part of perigynium (PO_0009044)
reason: In Carex floras (e.g. Flora of China) the 'utricle' is the perigynium. The winged, ciliate and serrulate upper margins are Carex. Caveat: this conflicts with R1192, where a bare 'utricle' is the utricle capsule fruit PO_0030097. Restrict to Cyperaceae.

target: pistillode (PO_0009078)
reason: Exact: the reduced, sterile gynoecium of a male flower is the pistillode, as for 'ovary rudiment' (R2956).
Generic part, as 'ultimate segment' was rejected in the 2026-11-13 review. It is the last division of a dissected leaf, leaflet or frond, and its organ must come from the context.
